(1) the influence-based approximation is effective, and (2) the common belief that the influence-based approximation will be more effective in the batch mode setting than the serial setting is not supported by the data.

(1) the influence of a data point on the retrained model is a good predictor of the sample's value to the model, and (2) the value of a data point to the model is often not well approximated by its value to a single goal.

(i) influence functions provide an effective and efficient approximation to goal-oriented AL strategies; (ii) the commonly used batch mode setting of AL is not suitable for such strategies; (iii) the common practice of using an ensemble of base models for active sampling is not beneficial in this setting; and (iv) the commonly assumed independence of the influence of a sample and its label is not always valid
